title: Peru vs Ecuador: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Peru and Ecuador for travelers, covering Machu Picchu vs Galápagos, costs, trekking, food, and Andean culture.

categories.title: 🍞 Food & Dining
categories.summary: Peru has one of the most celebrated food cultures on the planet. Lima holds three restaurants in the World's 50 Best Restaurant list — Central (which held #1 in 2023), Maido (Nikkei-Peruvian fusion), and Kjolle — alongside dozens of excellent mid-range options. categories.title: 🏛 Culture & History
categories.summary: Peru's historical depth is staggering. The Inca Empire — at its height in the early 16th century, the largest empire in pre-Columbian America — built Machu Picchu, Ollantaytambo, Pisac, and Sacsayhuamán with stones fitted so precisely that a knife blade cannot pass between them. categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Both countries are mid-range by South American standards — cheaper than Argentina (which has normalized recently) and Brazil for tourists, more expensive than Bolivia. categories.title: ☀️ Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Both countries straddle the equator and have complex microclimates determined by altitude and geography rather than traditional seasons. The Pacific coast, Andes, and Amazon all behave differently.

faqs.question: Is Peru or Ecuador better for the Galápagos?
faqs.answer: Ecuador wins by default — the Galápagos Islands are Ecuadorian territory. You fly from Quito or Guayaquil (2.5 hours). faqs.question: Is Peru or Ecuador cheaper?
faqs.answer: They're similar in overall cost. Both run $40-80/day for a mid-range independent traveler. Peru can be slightly more expensive around Cusco/Machu Picchu due to entry fees ($45-152 for Machu Picchu depending on circuit), but also has more budget options. faqs.question: Can you do Peru and Ecuador in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes — this is one of South America's great multi-country itineraries. A 3-4 week trip might cover: Quito → Galápagos (5-7 days) → Guayaquil → fly to Lima → Cusco → Machu Picchu → Sacred Valley. The Lima-Quito flight takes about 4 hours. Many travelers do the Gringo Trail: Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia in 4

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Peru vs Ecuador?
faqs.answer: Peru needs at least 10-14 days to do it justice: Lima, Cusco, Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, and ideally the Amazon or Lake Titicaca. Ecuador is more compact — 10 days covers Quito, Galápagos (5 days), and Baños or the Amazon. Neither feels rushed at 2 weeks; Peru especially rewards longer stays.

faqs.question: Which has better trekking — Peru or Ecuador?
faqs.answer: Peru is the king of Andean trekking. The Inca Trail (4 days, 43 km, ending at Machu Picchu's Sun Gate) is one of the world's great hikes but requires booking 5-6 months ahead. faqs.question: Is altitude sickness a concern in Peru vs Ecuador?
faqs.answer: Yes for both, but Peru has more high-altitude time. Cusco sits at 3,400m (11,200 ft), Machu Picchu at 2,430m, and the Inca Trail reaches 4,215m. Lake Titicaca is at 3,812m. faqs.question: Which country has better food — Peru or Ecuador?
faqs.answer: Peru wins — it's one of the world's great culinary destinations. Lima has multiple restaurants in the World's 50 Best list (Central, Maido, Astrid y Gastón).
